correctness.limitations: The replay certifies the finite witnesses, not the universal upper bound or the padding argument. Those were checked analytically.
correctness.rationale: For any query the positive branch in the full class is a translate of the centers of weight at most two. Within that branch, weights zero and above four are constant and weights three and four have at most six positive centers. For an intersection with a second ball centered at weight one, parameterize the centers by a free distinguished bit and at most one outsider. Queries with two or three outsiders have five or three positive centers; queries with one outsider have a negative branch in a translated star. For a second ball centered at weight two, the centers are arbitrary subsets of the two distinguished bits with no outsider, or exactly one distinguished bit with one outsider. Queries with zero or two distinguished bits have at most five positives when they split, while queries with one distinguished bit and zero or one outsider have star negative branches; with two or three outsiders they have at most three positives. A splitting query on a star has at most three positives, so stars have dimension at most two. These bounds yield depths at most three on the double intersections, four on a ball, and five on the full class. In d=3 and d=4 the negative root branch has 1 and 5 centers; in d=5 the 16-center positive root branch admits no 8/8 cut (intersection sizes 16,10,10,6,6,0). Independent verification checked all 58 certificate paths for depths 1,3,4,5 in dimensions 3,4,5,6; zero-padding proves all larger lower bounds. Distinctness and label consistency were both checked.
